newsitem.title: USA: World Bank approves China loans worth $830 mln.
newsitem.headline: World Bank approves China loans worth $830 mln.

text.p: The World Bank has approved two loans worth a total of $830 million for flood protection and for a thermal electric power plant in China.

A World Bank statement said the loans had been approved on Tuesday. The Bank would lend China $400 million for the Waigaoquiao power project and $430 million for flood protection, hydroelectric power and irrigation work on the Yellow River.
The loans bring the World Bank's China lending to $2.8 billion this financial year, or a total of around $28 billion since China joined the World Bank in 1981.
The Bank said its Waigaoquiao loan would fund part of the $1.9 billion thermal electric project, designed to help meet rising electricity demand in the fast-growing Shanghai region.
The hydroelectric loan would help fund the second part of a $2.2 billion project, financing the second stage of a dam and power plant.
It is the second World Bank loan for the project, which was started in 1993. The first loan was for $400 million.
